archetype: Naya Dinosaur typal ramp into a critical-mass board, v1.2.0: a ONE-CHANNEL deck again. The noncombat drain layer is gone and every route to a kill now runs through combat, so the currency is a Gishath hit and what multiplies it (double strike from Berserkers' Onslaught, a second trigger from Roaming Throne named Dinosaur, a copied Gishath via Sunfrill Imitator, size from Overwhelming Stampede and Kessig Wolf Run). The reveal puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield in batches, and the 99's entry payoffs turn each batch into cards and bodies. The climb was rebuilt on mana creatures: seven non-Dinosaur mana creatures plus Hulking Raptor and Regal Behemoth. Commander-reliant, though Natural Order, both Ghaltas, Carnage Tyrant, Zacama and Etali give the deck threats that do not need the command zone. Bracket floor 3 on three Game Changers (Enlightened Tutor, Natural Order, Worldly Tutor), zero contained combos (bracket_report.json, deck-facts).

role_assignment.default_role: CONTROL POSTURE for the climb, BEATDOWN from the first connect, and v1.2.0 made that a single line again. strategy:whos-the-beatdown's operational test is inevitability, 'whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown'; strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock adds that 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan'. This deck owns the long game only once the reveal is running, because with the noncombat drain cut there is no second clock that works without a combat step. So: hold the control posture while mana comes online, and switch to beatdown when Gishath can hit. The v1.2.0 climb is measurably faster (goldfish, 10,000 games, seed 42, sha d58a86fb): mean available mana 3.641 at turn 3, 6.98 at turn 6, 8.976 at turn 8; Gishath cast by turn 6 in 0.405 of games, mean turn 6.706, median 7, not cast by turn 10 in 1,396 of 10,000. The paired net-change against v1.1.0 is in the same direction: board power at turn 6 15.79 -> 20.34 (95% CI on the difference [+4.14, +4.97]) and killed by turn 6 0.092 -> 0.184 ([+0.084, +0.101]), against one goldfish opponent with no blockers. Who the deck is beatdown against depends on the seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown's Commander correction, 'assign per-threat, not per-game'). Captain's log 003 (on the v1.1.0 list) shows what it costs to get this wrong in a five-player pod: 'I didn't really do what I should have done to Alex because I was nervous about losing dinosaurs', and the pilot lost to the seat he left alone.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: A resolved Gishath that can hit this turn, with a protection spell you can cast after tapping out for him. strategy:pivot-point: 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after'. Flawless Maneuver is the one shield in the list that costs nothing once you control a commander (oracle text). strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the bar the table applies to you: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing'. The second trigger arrives once the reveal has resolved and the board outclasses the table. That is the pilot's repeated failure, recorded in two logs on two lists: log 002, '8-9 dinos with counters, 30+ power on board ... Should have swung everything at both'; log 003, 'I swung like two or three of them ... I should be feeding the dinos ... this is a creature deck'. strategy:combat-math.racing: 'the moment you stabilize, flip to offense to shrink the window in which they can draw out of it'. strategy:pivot-point: 'stop deploying the turn attrition starts favoring you'. Revealed Dinosaurs enter after attackers are declared, so they swing next turn. The pivot turn is therefore the turn AFTER the first big reveal: attack with everything, aimed where it kills a player, and keep one protection instant up.

engines.engine: THE PUT DOOR, in batches. Gishath reveals cards equal to the combat damage he deals and puts every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. The 99 holds 28 Dinosaur creature cards (enumerated from cards.json; Roaming Throne is a Golem in the library and is not one), so a 7-damage hit expects 7 x 28/99 = 1.98 Dinosaurs. The goldfish measures 2.02 per fire (5.226 bodies over 2.586 fires). He is the only thing that starts the engine, and he lives in the command zone, so he can never be revealed or tutored. Nothing worded 'if you cast it' fires off this door.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_metrics.commander_reveal declared, fired in 8,290 of 10,000 games, mean_fired 2.586, mean_bodies 5.226, connect rate 0.70/attack read from a V3 Forge run (432faa65) and therefore an authored rate on this list; engine.json ignition stage

engines.piece: Berserkers' Onslaught, Roaming Throne, Sunfrill Imitator, Kessig Wolf Run, Overwhelming Stampede
engines.engine: MULTIPLIERS ON THE ONE HIT. These five are what make one connect worth more than one reveal. By oracle text: Onslaught gives every attacker double strike, so Gishath deals combat damage in two steps and can trigger twice. Throne named Dinosaur makes other Dinosaurs' triggered abilities trigger an additional time, Gishath's included. Sunfrill Imitator can attack as a copy of Gishath, keeping its own name, which is a second creature carrying the reveal (log 003 records it, 'copied my commander, which was then allowing me to swing for 14'). Stampede adds the greatest power to every creature, so the reveal gets that much deeper too. Wolf Run is the one multiplier on a land, so a sweeper cannot take it. strategy:conversion.combat-channel says how combat pays in a pod: the fix is multiplicative, 'effects reading "each creature you control"'. strategy:conversion.raising-the-ceiling names extra combats and doublers as the levers once more swaps stop helping. None of the double-trigger readings is verified.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json lines ignition->wincon and conversion->ignition, both verified_by null; captain's log 003 (on the v1.1.0 list: a log, not a stack); goldfish meta combat_effects_not_modelled names Sunfrill Imitator, so the goldfish cannot see the copy

engines.piece: Pantlaza, Sun-Favored; Garruk's Uprising; Vaultborn Tyrant; Earthshaker Dreadmaw; Curious Altisaur; Trumpeting Carnosaur
engines.engine: ENTRY -> CARDS. This is the layer that turns a batch into a refill. Uprising and Vaultborn each draw for every entering creature with power 4 or greater. Dreadmaw draws one per other Dinosaur. Pantlaza discovers once a turn, at the entering creature's toughness. Carnosaur discovers 5. Curious Altisaur draws per Dinosaur that deals combat damage to a player. strategy:card-advantage.plan-draw puts the trade plainly: this is on-plan draw, which 'draws nothing in the engine-less hand and in bursts once the engine runs'. It fails when the plan fails, and the deck has no steady draw to cover the hands without the engine. Measured: extra cards drawn by turn 8 is 2.79 on the goldfish and did not move in the v1.2.0 merge (paired net-change 2.32 -> 2.31, a no-call). Selvala and Vaultborn are both named in draw_not_modelled, so both figures are floors.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_metrics.mean_extra_cards_drawn_by_turn['8'] 2.79; meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled [Jetmir's Garden, Selvala, Vaultborn Tyrant]; branches/jurassic-v1/net_change.json 'extra cards by T8' verdict noise

engines.piece: The mana-creature climb: Ixalli's Lorekeeper, Bloom Tender, Drover of the Mighty, Intrepid Paleontologist, Atzocan Seer, Faeburrow Elder, Selvala; Hulking Raptor, Regal Behemoth, Mirari's Wake
engines.engine: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB, moved onto bodies. v1.2.0 traded spell-based ramp and fixing for creatures. strategy:conversion.raising-the-ceiling is the reason: 'for a 6 mana commander, investing in cards and ramp is the only thing that lets us cast our commander at all'. The cost is the one strategy:conversion.durability prices: 'a creature converter dies to the same sweeper that kills the fodder'. Seven of the eleven non-Dinosaur creatures are mana creatures (enumerated), and none of them is protected by Temple Altisaur. Two of the mana sources are limited in what they pay for, and deck-facts reads the clauses: Ixalli's Lorekeeper pays only for Dinosaur spells and Dinosaur abilities, while Faeburrow Elder and Bloom Tender count colours among your permanents (mana_analysis credits both with no fixed colour). Mirari's Wake is the noncreature doubler and the table reads it as a tell: log 003, 'everybody's like, oh, that's going to be a problem'.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); deck-facts restricted_mana; mana_analysis producers; goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn 3.641 / 6.98 / 8.976 at turns 3 / 6 / 8; net-change 'hand can act by T3' 0.827 -> 0.863, CI [+0.026, +0.046]

engines.engine: A PUT-DOOR TUTOR that a mana creature pays for. Sacrifice a green creature and put a green creature card from the library onto the battlefield. 29 of the 39 creatures in the 99 are green (cards.json colours), including all six two- and three-mana Druid-type dorks, and the targets include Ghalta, Primal Hunger, Ghalta and Mavren, Vaultborn Tyrant, Carnage Tyrant and Zacama. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices it: a tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck', paid for with 'the less actual cards you get to play'. Natural Order puts the creature onto the battlefield, so Zacama arrives without its land untap. It is also one of the three Game Changers that set the bracket floor.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); bracket_report.json game_changers; engine.json line mana->fuel (verified_by null)

engines.piece: Regal Imperiosaur, Devil Dinosaur, Mirari's Wake, Rydia's Return, Overwhelming Stampede, Garruk's Uprising
engines.engine: THE ANTHEM LAYER, which the pilot asked to keep ('anthems fine', 2026-11-02). strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density measured it on this bench: a refactor that cut every lord and anthem dropped Forge combat damage from 29.07 to 18.20 per game, because 'a wide board of 1/1s is simply blocked'. strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density.lord-exposure prices the bodies: 'the body half of a lord is its cost'. Here the split is two creature lords (Imperiosaur, Devil Dinosaur) and four noncreature cards (Wake's static anthem, Uprising's trample, and the one-turn pumps Stampede and Rydia's Return mode one). The noncreature ones survive a sweeper. Devil Dinosaur also gives other Dinosaurs hexproof, which covers targeted removal only, not a sweeper.

engines.piece: Wipe protection: Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Eerie Interlude, Temple Altisaur, Vaultborn Tyrant
engines.engine: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER: the pilot's first ask. Enumerated by what each one stops, from oracle text. DESTROY sweepers: Flawless Maneuver (free with a commander), Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will (mode two: indestructible and protection from each colour). DAMAGE sweepers: those four, plus Temple Altisaur, which prevents all but 1 to your other Dinosaurs but not to itself or to the non-Dinosaur mana creatures. A DEATH you cannot stop: Vaultborn Tyrant leaves a token copy behind. EXILE, -X/-X, BOUNCE or SACRIFICE sweepers: only Eerie Interlude, which exiles your creatures and returns them at the next end step. Tokens it exiles do not come back. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math: 'buy resilience instead of restraint where you can'. The gap is breadth, not count: four of the five spells answer the same kind of sweeper, and one card covers all the others.
engines.evidence: oracle text for every card named (cards.json); goldfish target 'Protection held for the board' 0.717 assembled, 0.526 by turn 6, mean turn 3.859 (net_change blind_spots: the goldfish is never targeted, so protection reads as a dead card)

engines.piece: Recursion: Atzocan Seer, Intrepid Paleontologist, Rydia's Return (mode two), Vaultborn Tyrant
engines.engine: THE REBUILD: the pilot's second ask, and the thinnest part of v1.2.0. Enumerated from oracle text. Seer sacrifices itself to return a Dinosaur card from your graveyard to hand. Paleontologist exiles cards from graveyards for {2} and lets you CAST Dinosaurs it exiled from your own graveyard, each with a finality counter. Rydia's Return returns two permanent cards to hand at sorcery speed. Vaultborn copies itself once. strategy:conversion.durability names the flaw: 'a creature converter dies to the same sweeper that kills the fodder'. Seer and Paleontologist are 2/3 and 2/2 creatures, so they die in the same wipe and cannot reach Dinosaurs that died alongside them. Seer can only return a Dinosaur already in the graveyard before the wipe, and Paleontologist's exiled cards are tied to that one Paleontologist (needs a stack scenario). That leaves Rydia's Return as the only post-wipe recursion that is not a creature, at five mana, sorcery speed, two cards. strategy:conversion.availability ranks where an engine should sit: 'then an enchantment or artifact ... then recursion'.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); net_change blind_spots: 'nothing dies in a goldfish, so recursion has no target', so the goldfish cannot measure any of this

engines.piece: Wrathful Raptors, Temple Altisaur, Blasphemous Act
engines.engine: THE ENRAGE PACKAGE, now down to one payoff. Wrathful Raptors is the only enrage payoff left in the 99. Four sources can damage your own Dinosaur (Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth's ETB, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode, Zacama's {2}{R}; engine.json enumeration). Goldfish 'Enrage engine drawn' 0.407 assembled, 0.172 by turn 6, mean turn 6.335; the Act-plus-Altisaur pair 0.020 by turn 6. Log 002 already named the problem ('Enrage engine in Gishath is idling'). The Act-plus-Altisaur sweep is also less one-sided on v1.2.0: it now kills ten of the eleven non-Dinosaur creatures, all the mana creatures among them. Roaming Throne is the exception if it was named Dinosaur. Stack 004 verified this line on an older board holding a card not in this 99, so it is not cited as fact here.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish targets; engine.json output stage and open_questions[3]; stacks/004 checker pass on a non-v1.2.0 board

engines.piece: Bronzebeak Foragers, Thrashing Brontodon, Tranquil Frillback, Itzquinth, Zacama
engines.engine: REMOVAL ON DINOSAUR BODIES, so a reveal can deliver an answer for free. v1.2.0 improved interaction BREADTH. Enumerated by class: creature (Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Itzquinth, Trumpeting Carnosaur discard, Zacama {2}{R}, Bronzebeak, Blasphemous Act); artifact and enchantment (Thrashing Brontodon, which is a {1} instant-speed activation once on board, Tranquil Frillback, Zacama {2}{G}, Bronzebeak); graveyard (Tranquil Frillback, Intrepid Paleontologist). That is four of strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's five classes ('creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land'). LAND is the class nothing answers.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Re-resolve the core connect on v1.2.0-only cards
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: engine.json open_questions[0]: none of the five passing stacks has a board drawn only from this 99, so the deck's central line is unverified on v1.2.0. The questions to settle: entries happen at the same time, Uprising and Vaultborn each draw per power-4+ entry, Pantlaza discovers only once, and Earthshaker counts the other Dinosaurs that entered with it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Roaming Throne named Dinosaur doubles Gishath's reveal (and what it does to Pantlaza's once-a-turn)
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: 'If a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type triggers, it triggers an additional time.' Gishath is a Dinosaur, so one hit should produce two reveals of that many cards. Pantlaza's 'Do this only once each turn' probably makes the extra trigger do nothing after the first discover. engine.json open_questions[1].

candidate_missing_lines.title: Berserkers' Onslaught on Gishath: two damage steps, two reveals, 14 commander damage
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Double strike gives a first-strike damage step and a regular one, and each should fire a combat-damage trigger. Dinosaurs revealed in the first step enter after attackers were declared, so they do not attack. With Stampede, the reveal depth equals the pumped power. engine.json open_questions[2].

candidate_missing_lines.title: Sunfrill Imitator attacking as a copy of Gishath
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: on attack it becomes a copy of another Dinosaur you control, 'except its name is Sunfrill Imitator'. Because the names differ, the legend rule should not apply, and the copy should carry the reveal trigger. Log 003 says it happened ('swing for 14'). A log is not a stack, and the goldfish cannot see this card (combat_effects_not_modelled).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Eerie Interlude in response to an exile or sacrifice sweeper, as a rebuild AND an entry batch
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Interlude is the only card in the list that dodges an exile, -X/-X, bounce or sacrifice sweeper (enumerated above). Exiled tokens, such as Hatcher's Eggs and Regisaur or Ghalta tokens, cease to exist. The cards return together at the next end step, which should be one batch of entries for Vaultborn and Uprising draws plus one Pantlaza discover. That is the deck's best answer to a wipe and nothing verifies it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Intrepid Paleontologist as a CAST door: rebuying Zacama from your graveyard with its land untap
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Paleontologist lets you cast Dinosaur creature spells it exiled from cards you own. A cast satisfies Zacama's 'if you cast it', where Natural Order and Gishath's reveal do not. Open rules points: the finality counter, and whether cards exiled by a Paleontologist that left the battlefield stay castable (by CR 607 linked abilities they probably do not).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Natural Order off a mana creature into Ghalta, Primal Hunger or Vaultborn Tyrant
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The additional cost is to sacrifice a green creature, and Drover is green. The fetched creature is put onto the battlefield, so Vaultborn's own 'whenever this creature ... enters' should still trigger (draw, gain 3). The pick between a 12/12 trampler and a draw engine depends on the board, so a scenario helps.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur + Wrathful Raptors on a v1.2.0 board
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 004 passed on a board holding a card not in this 99 (engine.json open_questions[3]). On v1.2.0 the same sweep also kills the deck's own mana creatures. The re-resolution should count the redirected damage and the creatures you lose.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Still the worst matchup, and v1.2.0 made it worse in one specific way. The climb now sits on creatures, so a sweeper that used to cost you threats now costs you mana as well. strategy:conversion.durability: 'a creature converter dies to the same sweeper that kills the fodder'. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math sets the discipline: 'assume the wrath ... deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package, and when possible let another player's board be the reason it gets cast'. Its other instruction, 'buy resilience instead of restraint', is what the protection suite is for. Against destroy and damage sweepers the deck is well covered (Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Temple Altisaur). Against exile and -X/-X sweepers it has only Eerie Interlude. Hold it for that kind of sweeper rather than spending it on a destroy sweeper that indestructible already answers. Rebuild order follows the same section, 'redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper'. Kessig Wolf Run, Mirari's Wake and Garruk's Uprising survive a creature wipe and keep the next wave dangerous. Gishath's recast tax is the cost strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance names, '{2} per prior command-zone cast'. The pilot's own read (log 002) is the right one: 'holding creatures back through wipe waves is a real strategy, not just an accident.'
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit an eight-drop hardest. v1.2.0 answers with redundancy: the three Dinosaur cost reducers (Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator) plus Hunting Velociraptor's prowl, and enough mana creatures that one lost producer does not stop the climb. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial forces the role: 'you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion'. It also tells you to 'name your outs early'. Against an artifact or enchantment lock piece the outs are better than on v1.1.0: Thrashing Brontodon ({1}, sacrifice, instant speed once on board), Tranquil Frillback's ETB, Bronzebeak Foragers' ETB, and Zacama's {2}{G}. All four are creatures you have to resolve first. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: 'some answers must be castable under the tax', and a three-mana Brontodon is the cheapest. Against an effect that stops entry triggers, Gishath's reveal still puts bodies onto the battlefield, but every entry payoff goes quiet. Plan on the trample swing. Restricted mana matters here (deck-facts): Ancient Ziggurat, Cavern of Souls and Unclaimed Territory cannot pay for an activated ability. Secluded Courtyard and Ixalli's Lorekeeper can.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Hold the ground with size. Cheap Dinosaurs are big for their cost (Pugnacious Hammerskull 6/6 for three, Regal Imperiosaur 5/4 for three, Drover of the Mighty 3/3 with a Dinosaur). Temple Altisaur's damage floor blanks small attackers into your other Dinosaurs. strategy:card-advantage.virtual: 'A big blocker against an aggro deck turns their small creatures into dead cards', and in Commander 'virtual advantage triples'. Kinjalli's Sunwing makes their creatures enter tapped, which blanks haste (log 003 credited it). Take the control role and let the engine out-scale them (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The fragile piece is the mana creatures: an aggro seat's removal or blockers aimed at your 1/1 dorks slow the climb more than they would against a land-ramp list. Trade them only after Gishath is down.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Structurally weak, and the frame is short because the tools are. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now'. Instant-speed interaction is Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode, Boros Charm's 4 to a planeswalker, and on-board activations from Thrashing Brontodon and Zacama. There are no counterspells. Goldfish 'interaction castable' is 0.283 at turn 6 and 0.407 at turn 8, a floor, because the model taps out every turn. strategy:critical-mass gives the plan: 'the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers'. The faster v1.2.0 climb (killed by turn 6 0.092 -> 0.184, paired) is that defence. Race, and keep Brontodon on board against an artifact or enchantment combo. Log 002's loss to a drain seat while 30+ power sat on board is the warning: the race only works if you actually swing.
matchup_frames.vs_big_pod: Log 003 was a five-player game, and strategy:conversion.combat-channel names combat's three taxes in a pod: 'Three sets of blockers divide your width', an attack 'opens you to the two seats you did not choose', and 'the step comes once a turn'. A bigger pod makes all three worse, and with no noncombat clock left in v1.2.0 they bind. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management: 'who is the archenemy this turn, whose clock is fastest'. In log 003 the pilot named the right threat (Alex's growing artifact board) and did not attack it. strategy:combat-math.racing: 'races there are two-player subgames ... spend the minimum that wins yours'. Pick the seat whose board beats you, and kill it with everything.

distribution_notes: 93 entries / 100 copies, 36 land copies over 29 land entries, 64 nonland including the commander (deck-facts). Curve by mana value: 6 at one, 10 at two, 16 at three, 9 at four, 11 at five, 6 at six, 2 at seven, 1 at eight (Gishath), 2 at nine, 1 at twelve. The mode is still three, against strategy:deckbuilding.curve's 'modal mana value at 2'. v1.2.0 moved two cards into the two slot and took one each off three, four and eight. 39 creatures in the 99: 28 Dinosaurs and 11 others, 7 of which are mana creatures. strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density's floor is '30+ creatures', and 39 clears it. 28 Dinosaurs is the number that keeps the reveal at about two per seven damage (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors: '90% by ten cards seen costs about 20 copies'). The 11 non-Dinosaurs are dead cards to the reveal, and that is the tax the climb pays. Role histogram (deck-facts): ramp:dork 8, ramp:rock 3, ramp:land 3, ramp:cost-reduction 4; draw:engine 3, draw:impulse 2; removal:spot 5, removal:damage 4; protection:self 8, protection:granted 2; recursion 2; tutor:narrow 8. Against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' template ('36–38 lands, 10–12 ramp, 10 card draw, 10–12 targeted removal'), ramp is over, lands are at the floor, and draw is the short axis. The same section warns that templates 'are counts of functions, not cards': Pantlaza, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Etali and Trumpeting Carnosaur all generate cards without a draw tag. Mana (mana_analysis, sha d58a86fb): land sources W 16 / R 19 / G 28, total W 21 / R 24 / G 34. On-curve, lands only: W 0.81, R 0.548, G 0.785. With rocks and dorks: W 0.895, R 0.694, G 0.882. Red is still the binding colour, but the double-red cards are now at five and six mana (Berserkers' Onslaught, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Quartzwood Crasher, Etali, Trumpeting Carnosaur). For those, strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources asks 22 to 23 sources ('23 for 3{C}{C}, 22 for 4{C}{C}'), and the deck has 24 counting nonland, so the red problem has eased. Keeps follow strategy:mulligans.engine-hands, 'mulligan to enabler *classes*, not named cards'. Here the enabler class is mana, and with ramp or fixing drawn in 0.979 of games it is rarely the reason to ship a hand. Goldfish (10,000 games, seed 42, model a18364c317e2): first seven kept 0.787, mean mulligans 0.257, can act by turn 3 0.855; ramp or fixing drawn 0.979 (0.906 by turn 6, mean turn 2.018); Dinosaur payoff 0.885 / 0.654 / 3.924; connection kit 0.896 / 0.697 / 3.554; cost reducer or cheat 0.711 / 0.525 / 3.827; protection held 0.717 / 0.526 / 3.859; enrage engine 0.407 / 0.172 / 6.335; kill by turn 8 0.782, mean kill turn 7.494, median 7, no kill by turn 10 0.037. The goldfish has one opponent at 40 life and no blockers, so the kill turn is a clock, not a win rate. Unassisted figures are used throughout. Blind to this deck (net_change blind_spots, goldfish meta): protection, recursion, removal, and graveyard hate read as dead cards; draw from Selvala, Vaultborn and Jetmir's Garden is not modelled; combat effects of Etali, Pugnacious Hammerskull and Sunfrill Imitator are not modelled. FORGE HAS NEVER SEEN v1.2.0. Every Forge record is on an older list.
key_tensions: ONE CHANNEL. Cutting the drain layer for creatures made every kill depend on a combat step, so the pod's combat taxes (strategy:conversion.combat-channel) now apply to the whole plan. The deck's answer is to multiply the hit (double strike, Throne, the Imitator copy, Stampede), and none of those multipliers is verified or modelled.

THE CLIMB IS CREATURES, AND CREATURES ARE WHAT SWEEPERS KILL. Seven non-Dinosaur mana creatures die to every creature sweeper, including your own Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur. The faster climb (Gishath by turn 6 in 0.405 of games) is paid for in exposure to sweepers.

WIPE PROTECTION IS DEEP AGAINST ONE KIND OF SWEEPER AND THIN AGAINST THE REST. Four spells plus Altisaur cover destroy and damage sweepers. Exile, -X/-X, bounce and sacrifice sweepers are answered only by Eerie Interlude.
RECURSION IS ALMOST ALL ON CREATURES THAT DIE IN THE SAME WIPE. Rydia's Return is the only post-wipe recursion that is not a creature (strategy:conversion.durability).

THE PILOT'S MEASURED LEAK IS COMMITMENT, NOT CARDS. Logs 002 and 003, on two different lists, are both games lost with a dominant board that did not swing. strategy:pivot-point is the coaching, and no swap fixes it.
THREE LOGGED GAMES, 1W-2L, ALL ON SUPERSEDED LISTS (shas 0480aaf7, b394917f, 80701018), and none on v1.2.0.
overall_assessment: v1.2.0 plays the critical-mass game (strategy:critical-mass: 'every card feeds one plan, and the plan is reaching the threshold where the synergies take over'). Its threshold is a resolved Gishath that connects, with the next wave of Dinosaurs already on the battlefield. The merge went all in on the pilot's 'creatures through and through' direction. That cost the deck its noncombat clock and bought it a faster climb (paired against v1.1.0: board power at turn 6 +4.55, killed by turn 6 doubled from 0.092 to 0.184, hand can act by turn 3 +0.035) and multipliers on the one hit that matters. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry says which payoffs scale in a pod: 'wide alpha strikes ... commander-damage kills'. This list is now built for exactly those two, with the anthem layer (strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density) making the wide board connect, and Berserkers' Onslaught and Roaming Throne aiming at the commander-damage kill. The strategic cost is concentration. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection: 'built around your commander is not reliant on it'. With the drain layer gone, Gishath is again the only card that starts the engine. Natural Order into a Ghalta, Carnage Tyrant, Zacama and Etali are the threats that do not need the command zone. On the pilot's two asks, enumeration gives a split answer. WIPE PROTECTION is deep against destroy and damage sweepers and covered against everything else by one card, Eerie Interlude. RECURSION is thin: of the four cards, two are cheap creatures that die in the wipe they would recover from, and Vaultborn copies only itself, leaving Rydia's Return as the only recursion that is not a creature. strategy:conversion.durability and strategy:conversion.availability both say the same thing: the rebuild belongs on a type the sweeper does not read. That class of card is the clearest gap in the list. It is a class, not a named card, and it is not measurable on the goldfish, because nothing dies there. The rest is piloting. The pilot's logs say the leak is commitment, not cards. strategy:pivot-point ('recognizing it a turn early is a defining expert skill') and strategy:combat-math.racing ('the moment you stabilize, flip to offense') are the coaching. On this deck the pivot turn is the turn after the first big reveal: swing everything at the seat whose board beats you, with a protection instant up. What is missing is evidence, not theory. No passing stack names only v1.2.0 cards, Forge has never seen the list, and the double-trigger multipliers are unverified.
